Chapter 11 — The Cross and the Promise of Transformation.
Change... it’s never easy, is it? Old habits just seem to hang on, and sometimes, the comfort of what we already know can feel almost impossible to let go of. But here’s the amazing thing: the cross actually stands as a promise that real transformation is possible. Not just for you, but for your family, your community, and honestly—even for the world around us.
Think about the stories shared in this book. People who spent years trapped in bitterness, finally finding the courage to forgive. Friendships and families that seemed broken beyond repair, somehow being restored. Addictions, little by little, losing their hold. Hope, when it felt like it had vanished, coming back to life.
These aren’t tales of overnight miracles—they’re stories about the slow, steady work of grace. The cross is like a catalyst for this kind of change. Whenever you feel stuck, or weighed down by old patterns, it’s a reminder that new life is actually possible.
But where does transformation really start? It begins with honesty. With the courage to admit where we fall short, what we truly need, and that longing deep inside for something more. The cross opens up space for this kind of vulnerability. It assures us: you’re loved exactly as you are, but you’re also loved too much to stay the same.
Picture the moment when someone, after years of hiding, finally speaks their truth. There’s fear, sure, but on the other side? There’s freedom. That’s the kind of transformation the cross invites us into.
Most of us are scared of change. We worry about everything we might lose if we let go of the old ways. But the cross flips that question on its head. Instead of, “What might I lose?” it asks, “What might you gain?”
Imagine waking up with a deeper peace, a greater capacity to love, a life that’s truly filled with meaning and purpose. The journey isn’t always easy—far from it—but it’s always worth it.
